principles.statement: Untrusted input must be validated or sanitized before it influences a file path, command, or query.
principles.rationale: Unsanitized input is the root cause of injection and path-traversal vulnerabilities.

principles.statement: Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) must never appear as literals in source code.
principles.rationale: Source code is committed to history, copied, and shared far more widely and permanently than a config value or environment variable.

principles.statement: Error messages returned to an external caller should not expose internal implementation details.
principles.rationale: Stack traces, internal paths, and query text handed back to a caller give an attacker a map of the system's internals.

heuristics.name: Taint tracing
heuristics.description: Trace any value that originates from user input (request body, query params, file uploads, CLI args) forward to see where it's used — especially in paths, commands, or queries.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Reviewing any code that accepts external input.

decision_rules.condition: User-controlled input is used to construct a file path, shell command, or database query.
decision_rules.action: Verify it is validated/escaped/parameterized before use; flag it if not, naming the specific injection or traversal risk.

decision_rules.condition: A secret, API key, password, or token appears as a literal value in code.
decision_rules.action: Flag it — the value must be sourced from an environment variable or a config/secrets store instead.
exceptions: A clearly-labeled placeholder/example value in documentation or tests is not a real secret.

decision_rules.condition: An error response sent to an external caller includes a stack trace, internal file path, or raw query text.
decision_rules.action: Flag it and recommend returning a generic message while logging the detailed error only server-side.
exceptions: Verbose errors gated strictly behind a local/debug-only mode are acceptable.
